description.text: Guidewire is the platform that property and casualty (“P&C”) insurers rely on to engage with customers, innovate, and operate more efficiently. Founded in 2001, we serve insurers of all sizes, ranging from global carriers to regional and local providers, helping them navigate a rapidly changing insurance market. Our foundational core products, InsuranceSuite and InsuranceNow, are delivered as a cloud-based subscription service leveraging our proprietary cloud platform which we refer to as Guidewire Cloud Platform (“GWCP”). These products serve as transactional systems of record, fully supporting insurance operations, including product definition, pricing and rating, underwriting, policy administration, billing, and claims management. Our platform combines core systems of record with digital, analytics, and predictive and generative artificial intelligence (“AI”) capabilities. To support our core systems, we provide digital engagement offerings that enable seamless sales and pricing and rating solutions that enable sophisticated pricing models and streamlined rate logic deployment. Our platform provides enhanced claims experiences for policyholders, agents, vendors, and field personnel, and analytics products that allow insurers to manage and use data more effectively, gain business insights, improve operational efficiency, and underwrite emerging risks. To support insurers worldwide, we localize our products to address diverse regulatory, language, and currency requirements.

about.description_short: Guidewire is the platform P&C insurers trust to engage, innovate, and grow efficiently. More than 570 insurers in 44 countries, from new ventures to the largest and most complex in the world, rely on Guidewire products. With core systems leveraging data and analytics, digital, and artificial intelligence, Guidewire defines cloud platform excellence for P&C insurers. We are proud of our unparalleled implementation record, with 1,700+ successful projects supported by the industry's largest R&D team and consulting partner ecosystem. Our marketplace represents the largest partner community in P&C, where customers can access hundreds of applications to accelerate integration, localization, and innovation.

analysis_md:
# GWRE — Guidewire Software, Inc.
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-17. Price $168.86 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap (est) $14.422B — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json, or the FY2026 10-K balance sheet — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The dominant core-systems vendor for property & casualty insurers: InsuranceSuite (PolicyCenter, ClaimCenter, BillingCenter) and InsuranceNow on Guidewire Cloud Platform, plus newer pricing/AI products (PricingCenter, ProNavigator). Fiscal year ends July 31. FY2026: revenue $1,475,363,000 (+22.70% latest rev YoY per key_numbers.md), ARR $1.237B (+19% constant currency, per company Q4 FY2026 reporting), cloud ARR +35% to 84% of total ARR, subscription revenue rising as the on-prem license base migrates to cloud. FY2027 guidance (company): revenue $1.707B–$1.727B, ARR $1.45B–$1.46B (~18% constant-currency growth).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2026 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $389,716,000; capex $12,056,000; SBC $181,799,000 (always a real cost — 12.3% of revenue and the single biggest wedge between cash flow and owner's earnings).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2026: $195,861,000 = $2.29/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $2.29, latest FY OE total $195.9M)
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC, from financials_history.csv): $270,297,000 — higher than the conservative figure mainly because it does not deduct SBC in full; the conservative OCF-based figure is the one used.
- OE positive 3 of the last 5 fiscal years (key_numbers.md): OE/share was negative in the cloud-transition trough years (FY2022 −$2.21, FY2023 −$1.34 on the filed history) before turning positive in FY2024 ($0.52), FY2025 ($1.55) and FY2026 ($2.29).
- **Base used = normalized median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $1.55/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). No TTM override: the FY2026 10-K (filed 2026-09-11, period end 2026-07-31) is only 2.6 months old, there is no STALE_FY flag, and fundamentals.json's TTM through 2026-07-31 is the fiscal year itself. See BASE_DIVERGENCE below for why the median, not the latest year, is the base — and why the verdict does not depend on that choice.
- Balance sheet (FY2026 10-K): cash and equivalents $372,887,000; short-term investments $380,175,000; long-term investments $462,223,000; convertible senior notes, net $678,094,000 (long-term, the company's only funded debt); total liabilities $1,383,258,000 including current deferred revenue $437,181,000; stockholders' equity $1,193,687,000; lease liabilities $36,893,000 (dcf_numbers.json). Liquid assets plus investments exceed the converts — this is a net-cash balance sheet in substance, even though the engine cannot compute net debt (see DEBT_TAGS_BLANK). Buybacks were $606,309,000 TTM (fundamentals.json); shares outstanding fell to 81,992,669 (DEI, as of 2026-08-31) even as diluted weighted shares were 85,405,177.

## Moat: 6/10 — strong niche franchise, unproven through-cycle economics
Justification: Dominant P&C core platform (InsuranceSuite/Guidewire Cloud, 570+ insurers) with extreme switching costs — multi-year, mission-critical core replacements — and gross ARR attrition under 1.5% (under 1% for core customers) in FY2026. Capped at 6, not 7+: GAAP ROIC was negative through FY2024 and only inflected to +4.27% in FY2025 and +15.5% in FY2026 (fundamentals.json roic_proxy), so there is no through-cycle record of ROIC well above the cost of capital; the market is a narrow P&C-core niche contested by Duck Creek, Sapiens and Majesco, and long implementations carry execution risk.
- FOR: InsuranceSuite is the enterprise benchmark for large North American P&C carriers — PolicyCenter/ClaimCenter/BillingCenter on Guidewire Cloud; extreme switching costs (core-system replacements are multi-year, mission-critical programs); gross ARR attrition under 1.5% in FY2026, under 1% for core-system customers, 105 customers above $5M fully-ramped ARR; cloud ARR +35% in FY2026 to 84% of total ARR — the installed base is migrating onto its own cloud, deepening lock-in; expanding wallet share inside the base (PricingCenter — Nationwide as first US tier-1 customer; ProNavigator — 28 wins in FY2026).
- AGAINST: ROIC history is weak — roic_proxy (fundamentals.json) ran −5.55% (FY2021), −13.09% (FY2022), −9.88% (FY2023), −3.48% (FY2024), then +4.27% (FY2025) and +15.5% (FY2026), with no through-cycle proof; gross margin only just recovered to 64.2% in FY2026 from the 46.4% FY2022 cloud-transition trough (fundamentals.json annual gross margins: 52.4% FY2021, 46.4% FY2022, 50.6% FY2023, 59.5% FY2024, 62.5% FY2025, 64.2% FY2026); narrow TAM (P&C core only, finite pool of large-carrier replacements/migrations); credible challengers (Duck Creek modular cloud, Sapiens unified suite, Majesco, SI-led modernization); long services-heavy implementations; SBC of $181,799,000 in FY2026 (12.3% of revenue) caps owner's earnings.
- The written reason the measured ROIC history understates the franchise, in part: FY2021–FY2024 GAAP results carried the double cost of running on-prem and cloud estates through the transition plus heavy SBC, while gross margin and operating margin (−24.5% FY2022 to +10.2% FY2026, fundamentals.json) were mechanically depressed. That argues the forward franchise is better than the backward ROIC — but one year at +15.5% is an inflection print, not a cycle, so the score stays at 6.
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 9.8 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (engine 5.4.0)
Growth sanity check: the engine blend is 18.89% (components: rev CAGR 5y 14.70%, rev CAGR 3y 17.67%, latest rev YoY 22.70%, OE/share CAGR 2y 109.78%). The OE/share CAGR is an inflection artifact off the negative/trough base and is not taken at face value; the revenue components are the meaningful signal. Against actual prints: FY2026 revenue +22.70%, Q4 FY2026 revenue +15.3% YoY (company reporting), ARR +19% constant currency, cloud ARR +35%, and FY2027 guidance of ~16–17% revenue growth and ~18% ARR growth. The base start of 18.9% sits between the latest FY print and the FY2027 guide — defensible for OE/share, which also gets operating leverage as margins normalize, and it is not below what the company just printed. The bull start (23.9%) is slightly above the latest FY revenue print (22.70%): written reason — fully-ramped ARR grew +22% and cloud ARR +35% in FY2026, so a bull case in which cloud mix lifts OE/share growth modestly above the last revenue print is the correct shape of a bull case, not an error. The super-bull start (30.9%) exceeds every consolidated print: it is a 10%-probability tail that requires cloud ARR growth to convert into consolidated OE/share growth, and it still only yields a 7.52% IRR at this price. Default offsets (−12/−5/0/+5/+12pp) and OE multipliers (0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25) were kept; probabilities were shifted bear-ward (15/30/30/15/10 vs the 10/25/30/25/10 default) per the OE_VOLATILE instruction to widen bear weight.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | 6.9% | 0.75 | ARR growth decays to high single digits; SBC stays heavy; migration tail disappoints | $11.63 | 3.42% |
| Bear | 30% | 13.9% | 0.90 | Growth settles at/below the FY2027 guide and margins stall | $19.03 | 4.13% |
| Base | 30% | 18.9% | 1.00 | Blend growth decays normally over the 9.8-yr CAP | $26.37 | 4.85% |
| Bull | 15% | 23.9% | 1.10 | Cloud mix and operating leverage hold growth above the last print | $36.11 | 5.78% |
| Super bull | 10% | 30.9% | 1.25 | Cloud ARR converts to consolidated OE/share compounding | $55.55 | 7.52% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $26.34 (−84.4% vs price), IV@12% $36.45, IV@10% $47.92, weighted IRR 4.88%, base-case IRR 4.85%**
- **Tier by numbers: D — and the bear and bull tiers are both D** (IRR band: bear 4.13% → bull 5.78%; full scenario range 3.42%–7.52%). Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 0.92%, terminal value 23.0% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.78x, 2.6 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): 15% at $26.34, 20% at $17.51, 25% at $12.83.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years): real and structural, not noise — it is the cloud transition: OE/share went from −$2.21 (FY2022) and −$1.34 (FY2023) to +$2.29 (FY2026) on the filed history as gross margin recovered from 46.4% to 64.2%. Handled by the normalized 3-yr median base plus bear-widened probabilities (15/30 on super-bear/bear).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2024, 2025, 2026): explained — it is SBC, not a one-off tax deposit or impairment. Net income vs OCF on the filed history: FY2024 −$6,103,000 vs $195,748,000 with SBC of $146,460,000; FY2025 $69,804,000 vs $300,867,000 with SBC of $161,556,000; FY2026 $139,283,000 vs $389,716,000 with SBC of $181,799,000. In each year the non-cash SBC add-back accounts for most of the gap, with D&A and deferred-revenue/working-capital moves making up the rest. Consequence: the divergence does not flatter the base — the conservative OE definition deducts SBC in full, which is exactly why OE is so far below OCF.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK**: resolved from the filing. The engine found no LongTermDebt tag for FY2025–FY2026 because Guidewire's funded debt is tagged as convertible senior notes, not LongTermDebt. FY2026 10-K balance sheet: convertible senior notes, net $678,094,000 (long-term), against cash $372,887,000 + short-term investments $380,175,000 + long-term investments $462,223,000, with lease liabilities of $36,893,000. Balance-sheet verdict: net cash in substance; no leverage risk in the verdict. Net debt in the engine/score stays null (unknown to the engine), and no net-debt figure is quoted as computed.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY $2.29 vs 3-yr median $1.55): both are "real"; they measure different things. The median is dragged by the FY2024 trough year ($0.52), which sits inside the 3-yr window, so the median understates the current run-rate; the latest year is the first clean post-transition year and may overstate the through-cycle run-rate if FY2026 margins prove peak. The median was kept as the conservative base. Method range: re-running the same scenarios on the latest-FY base would scale IVs by roughly the base ratio — the weighted IV@15% would still sit in the tens of dollars against a $168.86 price, so the tier is D on either base. (Stated in words, not as a computed figure — no engine run was made on the alternate base.)
- **LOW_OE_YIELD** (base OE yield 0.92%): agreed — at $168.86 the valuation rests almost entirely on future growth and margin expansion, not on current owner's earnings. This is the core of the verdict: even the super-bull path (30.9% growth start, 1.25x OE) yields only a 7.52% IRR.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.78x super-bear IV): real — the outcome range is wide because the base is small and the growth path is contested. Confidence is capped at medium (never high with this flag), and the verdict is sized to the conservative end; the saving grace is that every scenario, super bull included, lands in Tier D at this price.

## My thoughts / overlay
- Quality is not the debate. This is a genuinely strong niche franchise — dominant P&C core platform, <1% core attrition, cloud migration largely self-cannibalizing onto its own platform, net-cash balance sheet, $606,309,000 of TTM buybacks shrinking the count. The debate is purely price: $168.86 capitalizes decades of flawless compounding that the owner's-earnings math cannot produce even in the super-bull case.
- The market is pricing the non-GAAP story (non-GAAP operating income and FCF before SBC). On the sweep's rules SBC is a real cost — $181,799,000 in FY2026 — and once it is charged, OE/share is $1.55 normalized / $2.29 latest against a $168.86 price.
